questions.stem: In triangle $PQR$, $p = 8\text{ cm}$, $q = 12\text{ cm}$, and $P = 35°$. Which expression finds angle $Q$?
questions.explanation: Using the sine rule for finding angles: $\frac{\sin Q}{q} = \frac{\sin P}{p}$, so $\sin Q = \frac{q \sin P}{p} = \frac{12 \sin 35°}{8}$.

questions.stem: When can the sine rule be used?

options.text: When you know all three sides
When you know at least one side and its opposite angle, plus one other piece of information
Only when all angles are known

questions.explanation: The sine rule requires a known pair of a side and its opposite angle, plus at least one other side or angle to find the unknown.

questions.stem: In triangle $ABC$, $A = 30°$, $C = 80°$, and $c = 15\text{ cm}$. What is the value of $B$, and which expression gives side $a$?
questions.explanation: $B = 180° - 30° - 80° = 70°$. By the sine rule: $a = \frac{c \sin A}{\sin C} = \frac{15 \sin 30°}{\sin 80°}$.
